narrativeReportMd:
# CatalogEntry R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`CatalogEntry` is a hard breaking removal from the R6 core resource set. Existing R4 instances with `resourceType: "CatalogEntry"` have no same-named R6 StructureDefinition and will not validate as R6 resources.

## Scope
The analysis compared the R4 `CatalogEntry` StructureDefinition to the R6 core package. Because the assigned R6 StructureDefinition is absent, I searched the R6 package index and related catalog artifacts. R6 contains `CatalogEntry` only as an old resource name in `CodeSystem-fhir-old-types`; it does not provide a direct resource, ConceptMap, or obvious one-to-one replacement in the supplied package.

## Main migration themes
The main issue is not a narrow element change but loss of the entire wrapper resource. R4 `CatalogEntry` carried per-catalog-item metadata such as `orderable`, `referencedItem`, identifiers, classification, publication status, validity dates, and entry-to-entry relationships. R6 still has many of the target item resources and a `catalog` profile on `Composition`, but those do not preserve the R4 wrapper semantics without an explicit migration design.

## Highest-impact findings
The resource identity removal is the highest-impact finding. A second high-impact issue is lossy conversion: data that was local to `CatalogEntry` has to move into item-specific resources, a catalog `Composition`, extensions, or profiles. A third issue is the removal of the self-referential `relatedEntry` graph and its required `relation-type` terminology.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for choosing the replacement modeling pattern. The local package evidence confirms removal, but it does not say whether HL7 intended `Composition` catalog profiles, item-specific definitional resources, extensions, or implementation-guide-specific profiles to carry each R4 field.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Given that R4 `CatalogEntry` was trial-use/FMM 0, removal may be justified, but the supplied inputs do not include the rationale. A less disruptive design would have retained a deprecated compatibility resource or supplied a formal cross-version mapping.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze the `catalog` Composition profile and any implementation-guide profiles that used R4 `CatalogEntry`. Also analyze target resources separately, because migrating `referencedItem` depends on the target resource type.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `CatalogEntry` is removed from R6 core, so R4 instances are hard-breaking at the resource identity level. The top migration concerns are replacing the wrapper resource, preserving per-item catalog metadata, and remapping `relatedEntry` relationships. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official replacement/migration map.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is likely model redesign rather than field renaming. Systems must decide whether each R4 `CatalogEntry` becomes metadata on the referenced item, an entry in a catalog `Composition`, an extension-bearing profile, or an implementation-guide-specific wrapper. Relationship semantics such as `triggers` and `is-replaced-by` need explicit mapping because the R4 self-reference and relation-type terminology are not present as R6 core CatalogEntry features.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the resource is absent: the assigned R6 StructureDefinition file is missing, the R6 package index has no exact `CatalogEntry` StructureDefinition, and R6 `CodeSystem-fhir-old-types` explicitly lists `CatalogEntry` as an old resource name. Confidence is medium for replacement guidance because no official diff, ConceptMap, or narrative migration note was available.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: A same-canonical or same-type match was not found. The only direct R6 occurrence of `CatalogEntry` is the old-types terminology marker, so the most reliable conclusion is deletion or non-one-to-one replacement rather than a simple rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct resource-level validation break. An R4 instance with `resourceType: "CatalogEntry"` has no R6 resource definition to validate against. R6 parsers, validators, generated SDKs, schema generators, REST endpoints, and switch statements over known resource types are likely to reject or omit `CatalogEntry` unless they include an explicit R4 compatibility layer.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Catalog entries can represent orderability and catalog availability for medications, devices, services, protocols, and other items. Dropping the wrapper without preserving its semantics can create catalog/business-rule errors even if the referenced item resource still exists.

justification.inferredGoal: Remove or replace a low-maturity catalog wrapper resource from the core resource set.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain CatalogEntry in R6 core as a deprecated compatibility resource while steering new implementations to the preferred catalog patterns.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 package decisively removes `CatalogEntry` and marks it as an old type; R4 also labeled it trial-use/FMM 0. Retiring a low-maturity wrapper from core is a reasonable goal, but the break is severe and the local inputs do not include an official rationale or replacement map. The partial alternative would reduce breakage but materially weakens model cleanup, so the breaking design is probably, not conclusively, justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept the same `resourceType` and element shape as a deprecated or legacy R6 core resource, with clearer definitions and warnings that newer catalog patterns are preferred. This is a true base-design alternative, unlike conversion tooling or an external profile. It would preserve validation of most R4 instances, but it risks old and new catalog representations coexisting indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves most R4 instances but keeps an FMM 0 generic wrapper in core, creates duplicate catalog representations, and may require indefinite validator and API support.

findings.narrativeMd: `CatalogEntry` has been removed from the R6 core resource set. This is not a field-level rename: R6 has no same-canonical or same-type resource definition for instances whose top-level `resourceType` is `CatalogEntry`. Any implementation that validates instances against R6 core definitions, generates R6 model classes, or exposes resource-type-specific REST behavior will need explicit compatibility handling.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `CatalogEntry` instance can become R6-invalid solely because the resource type is unknown in R6 core. Strict JSON/XML parsers generated from R6 are likely to reject it before evaluating child elements. This finding is primarily R4-to-R6; R6-to-R4 representability is not directly applicable because there is no R6 `CatalogEntry` instance shape.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not attempt an automatic same-name upgrade. Inventory existing R4 `CatalogEntry` instances, classify them by `referencedItem` target type and catalog use case, and select a replacement modeling pattern. Common choices may include putting metadata on the referenced item resource, using the `catalog` Composition profile for catalog-level grouping, or defining cross-version extensions/profiles. Regression tests should include parsers, validators, API resource-type dispatch, and code generation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because `CatalogEntry` was low-maturity in R4, removal may have been considered acceptable, but it remains technically breaking. A backward-compatible path could have preserved the resource as deprecated or supplied a formal migration package. The tradeoff is that keeping an obsolete resource in core can impede model cleanup and confuse implementers about preferred R6 patterns.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The package evidence is decisive for absence, but not for intended replacement. A human reviewer should look for ballot change notes or tracker discussions before finalizing migration guidance.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 defined `CatalogEntry` as a concrete `DomainResource`, while the supplied R6 package has no same-canonical StructureDefinition and marks `CatalogEntry` only as an old resource type. An R4 instance with `resourceType: "CatalogEntry"` is therefore an old-valid/new-invalid instance and generated R6 SDKs, validators, and REST handlers will not have a normal CatalogEntry surface. That is a real hard break, but the R4 artifact was FMM 0/trial-use, and a lightweight public-use check found removal/additional-resource material rather than clear evidence of broad production deployment. On that record, retiring the low-maturity core resource appears proportionate.

findings.title: CatalogEntry's per-item wrapper metadata has no direct R6 resource carrier

oldState.summary: R4 CatalogEntry carried local per-item catalog metadata.
oldState.narrativeMd: Local R4 elements included `identifier`, `type`, mandatory `orderable`, mandatory `referencedItem`, `additionalIdentifier`, `classification`, `status`, `validityPeriod`, `validTo`, `lastUpdated`, `additionalCharacteristic`, `additionalClassification`, and `relatedEntry`.

newState.summary: No single R6 core resource/profile was identified that preserves the CatalogEntry wrapper element set.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 retains many resources that R4 `referencedItem` could point to, and it retains a `catalog` profile on `Composition`, but those artifacts do not provide a same-shape per-item wrapper. The R6 `catalog` profile is catalog/document-level and was already present in R4.

facts.note: Count includes local CatalogEntry elements and local relatedEntry children, excluding inherited Resource/DomainResource/Element children.
`relatedEntry` is optional, but its children are mandatory when a related entry is present.
The R4 referencedItem target resources were found in R6, but they are the item resources, not a universal CatalogEntry wrapper.
Related catalog infrastructure exists but is not a same-type replacement for per-item CatalogEntry metadata.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The likely migration target is use-case-dependent. The presence of R6 item resources and the catalog Composition profile suggests possible modeling destinations, but no one-to-one element match is available in the supplied core package.

impact.impactRationaleMd: For R4-to-R6, every local `CatalogEntry` field is nested under a removed resource type, so an instance cannot be carried forward without transformation. For R6-to-R4, any replacement representation using `Composition`, item-specific resources, or extensions may not map cleanly back to the R4 wrapper fields. The validation break is certain, while the degree of data loss depends on the migration pattern chosen.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The lost wrapper fields include orderability, status, validity, classification, and item identity. These can drive formulary, catalog, ordering, and availability decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace a generic catalog wrapper with more specific resource models or profile-based catalog composition.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the deprecated CatalogEntry wrapper as the base compatibility carrier for per-entry metadata, rather than relying only on profiles, extensions, or a ConceptMap.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: R4 per-item catalog metadata loses its direct R6 carrier because the whole wrapper resource was removed. Moving away from a generic low-maturity wrapper toward more specific resource or Composition-based modeling is plausible. Ordinary extensions, profiles, and ConceptMaps help migration but do not themselves make R4 instances valid R6 base instances. The less-breaking base alternative is therefore only partial because it preserves data by retaining the old wrapper while creating real source-of-truth and interoperability costs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base design could have retained `CatalogEntry` with its local metadata as a deprecated compatibility resource. That would preserve most R4-valid instances and avoid forcing every implementation to invent a field-by-field carrier. The tradeoff is substantial: the same catalog facts could live in `CatalogEntry`, in a catalog `Composition`, or on item-specific resources, making validation and synchronization ambiguous and allowing the deprecated representation to accumulate indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids data loss for orderability, status, validity, classifications, and identifiers, but duplicates metadata across the wrapper, catalog Composition entries, and item resources.

evidence.detail: R4 defines local wrapper elements including identifiers, type, orderability, referenced item, classifications, status, validity dates, update date, characteristics, and related entries.
`orderable` and `referencedItem` are mandatory local elements in R4.
R6 has a `catalog` profile on `Composition`, with catalog-level constraints such as a validity-period extension, fixed `Composition.type` text `Catalog`, required `category`, and required `date`.
The `catalog` profile already existed in R4, so the R6 profile is not simply a new renamed CatalogEntry resource.
evidence.quote: R4 catalog profile constrained Composition.section.entry to Reference(CatalogEntry).

evidence.locator: R6 package search for catalog mentions and target resources
evidence.detail: R6 contains target item resources such as Medication, Device, HealthcareService, ActivityDefinition, PlanDefinition, SpecimenDefinition, ObservationDefinition, and Binary, but no universal CatalogEntry wrapper.

examples.examplesMd: This illustrative R4 fragment shows wrapper metadata that is not just part of the referenced item. In R6 it requires an explicit mapping decision; blindly replacing the resource type with a target item resource would lose catalog-specific semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 `CatalogEntry` was a wrapper around an item. Removing the resource removes the standard place where systems stored catalog-specific metadata independent of the referenced item itself. That matters because the same item can appear in different catalogs with different orderability, status, validity, classification, or identifiers.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using these fields are invalid as R6 because the containing resource type is absent. Even if a migration chooses an R6 `Composition` catalog or the target item resource, R6 validation will check a different element model. A generated R6 class model also will not expose `CatalogEntry.orderable` or `CatalogEntry.referencedItem`, so application logic must be rewritten rather than recompiled.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build an explicit field-by-field migration matrix. Treat `referencedItem` as the anchor to the actual catalog item, then decide where each wrapper field belongs. Test at least these cases: multiple CatalogEntry records pointing to the same item with different metadata, entries with no optional metadata, entries with validity/status data, and entries with implementation extensions. If no lossless R6 core location exists, preserve data with governed extensions or retain the original R4 instance alongside the R6 representation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible alternative would have left the wrapper available as deprecated or supplied official extensions on catalog `Composition.section.entry` or referenced resources. This would have reduced migration ambiguity. The cost would be maintaining a generic wrapper that may overlap with more precise R6 resource-specific models.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The finding intentionally does not claim a single official replacement because the supplied R6 package does not provide one. Human review should verify whether external ballot notes identify one.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The affected R4 paths are the local wrapper fields such as mandatory `orderable` and `referencedItem`, plus status, validity, identifiers, classifications, and characteristics. R6 retains a catalog profile on `Composition`, but that profile is catalog/document-level and does not provide a same-shape per-item wrapper; its R4 predecessor already existed and pointed section entries at CatalogEntry. Implementations that used these fields must choose a new representation and may need human mapping, especially when catalog-specific metadata differs from the referenced item. Even so, the carrier being removed was FMM 0/trial-use, and retaining the whole wrapper just to carry these fields would perpetuate a low-maturity duplicate model.
keyEvidence: R4 CatalogEntry local elements include orderable 1..1 boolean and referencedItem 1..1 Reference, plus status, validityPeriod, validTo, lastUpdated, identifiers, classifications, and characteristics.
R6 StructureDefinition-catalog is a profile on Composition with catalog-level constraints such as type, category, date, and a validity-period extension.
R4 StructureDefinition-catalog already existed and constrained Composition.section.entry to Reference(CatalogEntry), so the R6 catalog profile is not a direct renamed CatalogEntry carrier.
R6 Composition.section.entry is a generic Reference(Resource), not a per-entry metadata backbone.
No clear public production-use evidence was found in the lightweight check.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low FMM softens the concern despite the awkward migration. The fields can be business-relevant, but absent evidence that this FMM 0 wrapper was widely deployed, the break is more a migration burden than a standards stability failure.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss and old-valid/new-invalid: R4 wrapper metadata has no direct R6 core carrier, so R4 instances fail as-is and transformed R6 representations may not round-trip to the original CatalogEntry fields without implementation-specific choices.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping a deprecated CatalogEntry wrapper would preserve the field set and reduce mapping ambiguity, but it would also leave multiple possible sources of truth for the same catalog facts across the wrapper, Composition sections, and item resources. Extensions or ConceptMaps help migration but are not less-breaking base R6 designs because they do not make R4 CatalogEntry instances valid R6 resources.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing High impact description is accurate for implementations that used these fields, and the deprecated-wrapper alternative is only partial; however, FMM 0 and lack of clear production-use evidence make the break probably acceptable rather than a clear Revisit.

findings.title: CatalogEntry related-entry graph and relation-type terminology are not preserved in R6 core

oldState.summary: R4 allowed CatalogEntry-to-CatalogEntry relationships with required relation type and target item.

binding.description: The type of relations between entries.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 CodeSystem is complete locally with two concepts. R6 has no same-named ValueSet or CodeSystem file in the supplied core package.

oldState.narrativeMd: `CatalogEntry.relatedEntry` was optional, but when present it required `relationtype` (`triggers` or `is-replaced-by`) and `item`, a Reference to another `CatalogEntry`.

newState.summary: R6 has no CatalogEntry self-reference or same relation-type terminology in core.
newState.narrativeMd: Because `CatalogEntry` itself is absent, R6 has no `CatalogEntry.relatedEntry.item` target. The package also lacks `ValueSet-relation-type.json` and `CodeSystem-relation-type.json`. Broader relationship mechanisms such as `Composition.relatesTo` are not a direct replacement for a per-entry relationship graph.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old self-reference cannot be matched because the target resource is removed. R6 has general artifact/document relationship mechanisms, but the supplied inputs do not show an official match for the two CatalogEntry-specific relation codes.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance with `relatedEntry` depends on a self-reference to another `CatalogEntry` and a required CatalogEntry-specific relation code. With the resource and terminology gone from R6 core, relationship graphs cannot be mechanically validated or round-tripped. The runtime risk is high for catalog applications that use these links to trigger activities or replace retired items.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Relationship loss can affect replacement/substitution and triggered-activity behavior. The clinical or business severity depends on whether implementations used `relatedEntry` for ordering, formulary replacement, or workflow automation.

justification.inferredGoal: Retire CatalogEntry-specific relationship modeling along with the resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep relatedEntry and the relation-type codes only within a deprecated CatalogEntry compatibility resource, with optional mapping to broader R6 relationship mechanisms.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: `relatedEntry` was tightly coupled to a CatalogEntry-to-CatalogEntry graph, so removing it follows naturally if the low-maturity resource is retired. The old report's mapping or ConceptMap idea is not by itself a backward-compatible base design because it would not preserve R4 instance validation. A deprecated compatibility resource and retained terminology would be less breaking, but the tradeoffs are material enough that the removal is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would keep `CatalogEntry.relatedEntry` plus the `relation-type` ValueSet/CodeSystem as deprecated parts of the compatibility resource, while documenting optional mappings to `Composition.relatesTo` or artifact relationship codes. Keeping only a ConceptMap or extension would be migration support, not base compatibility. The remaining cost is maintaining an obsolete self-reference model and small terminology surface, with possible semantic drift and duplicate relationship channels in R6 implementations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Improves graph fidelity but keeps obsolete self-references and deprecated terminology in core; mapping to broader relationship types is incomplete, especially for triggers.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows an R4 entry that points to another CatalogEntry as a replacement. R6 core has neither the target resource type nor the same local relation field.

findings.narrativeMd: `relatedEntry` is a separate migration concern because it encoded a graph of catalog entries, not just metadata about a single item. Removing `CatalogEntry` also removes the stable target type for those links and the required local vocabulary that distinguished triggers from replacement.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `relatedEntry` is invalid in R6 for the same resource-removal reason, and its relationship details are not automatically representable elsewhere. Even if links are migrated to `Composition.relatesTo` or resource-specific references, validators will apply different target profiles and terminology bindings. Round-tripping back to R4 would require retaining the original relation code and target CatalogEntry identity.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Extract relationship edges before transforming entries. For each edge, preserve source entry identity, target entry identity, and relation code. Define a governed mapping for `triggers` and `is-replaced-by`; if no exact R6 relationship code exists, use extensions or retain the original R4 relationship alongside the R6 representation. Include tests for replacement chains and triggered-activity links.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This could have been less disruptive if the relation terminology had remained available as deprecated and if a ConceptMap had mapped CatalogEntry relationships to R6 artifact or document relationships. That would not solve every modeling difference, but it would make the semantic loss explicit and machine-testable.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A terminology server or official migration guide could reveal a preferred target for these two codes. None was found in the supplied core package.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `CatalogEntry.relatedEntry` was an optional R4 graph edge, but when present it required a `relationtype` code and a Reference to another CatalogEntry. R6 has no CatalogEntry target and the supplied core package has no same relation-type CodeSystem or ValueSet. A catalog application using `is-replaced-by` or `triggers` links would need an explicit redesign, and `triggers` in particular is not obviously preserved by broader R6 relationship machinery. Still, this path is optional, tightly coupled to the removed FMM 0 resource, and preserving it in core would mainly mean preserving the obsolete resource graph.

That would preserve graph fidelity, but at the cost of maintaining obsolete self-references and duplicate relationship channels; a ConceptMap alone would be migration aid, not base compatibility.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: No CatalogEntry-specific invariant was found beyond inherited `Element`, `Extension`, and `DomainResource` constraints. Inherited/base constraints are out of scope and the resource removal is captured separately.

The R4 CatalogEntry local elements did not define fixed, pattern, or default values. The R6 `catalog` Composition profile has fixed catalog document type text, but that belongs to the related profile rather than the assigned CatalogEntry resource.
No CatalogEntry-local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraints were identified in R4. There is no independent local value-limit breaking change apart from resource removal.
R4 CatalogEntry's local content elements were not marked as modifiers. Inherited modifier elements such as `implicitRules` and `modifierExtension` are excluded by the base-artifact scope rule.
No CatalogEntry-local slicing was identified in R4. Slicing in the related `catalog` Composition profile is out of scope for this resource report.

R4 local cardinalities were inspected, including mandatory `orderable` and `referencedItem`. No element-by-element R6 cardinality comparison is possible because there is no R6 CatalogEntry StructureDefinition.
R4 local types were inspected. R6 still contains the referenced item resource types, but no R6 CatalogEntry element tree exists for direct type-domain comparison.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 keeps CatalogEntry only as an old resource-type code
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This marker is not a functional replacement resource and does not by itself create additional instance breakage beyond the resource removal.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The marker is useful for compatibility tooling: systems can recognize that `CatalogEntry` is a historical FHIR resource name and route such instances to an R4 compatibility or migration path.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R4 referencedItem target resource types mostly remain present in R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The referenced item resources checked from the R4 target list are present as R6 StructureDefinitions, so the target item instances may have their own migration path. This does not preserve the removed CatalogEntry wrapper.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Use `referencedItem` to group migration work by target resource type. Each target resource must still be assessed under its own R4-to-R6 report.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: A catalog Composition profile exists in both R4 and R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The profile's existence is not a CatalogEntry breaking change because it was already present in R4 and is a constraint on `Composition`, not a replacement `CatalogEntry` resource.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The profile may still be relevant for catalog-level migration, especially where R4 catalog Compositions had sections pointing to CatalogEntry resources.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: The R4 `catalog` Composition profile referenced `CatalogEntry` entries, while R6 retains the catalog profile without a CatalogEntry resource. A profile-specific analysis should determine whether catalog-level documents need separate migration rules.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: Medication, Device, Organization, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, HealthcareService, ActivityDefinition, PlanDefinition, SpecimenDefinition, ObservationDefinition, Binary
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R4 `CatalogEntry.referencedItem` points to these resource types. Migrating a CatalogEntry requires separately valid R6 representations of the referenced item resources.

R4 `CatalogEntry.relatedEntry.relationtype` used this complete CodeSystem. R6 core does not include the same terminology file, so a terminology or ConceptMap follow-up is needed for relationship-preserving migrations.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The assigned R6 `CatalogEntry` StructureDefinition is absent. This makes the resource-removal finding high confidence but prevents a normal element-by-element R4/R6 comparison.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official R6 replacement StructureDefinition, deprecation note, or migration guide would clarify intended mapping semantics.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official ConceptMap or field-level migration table from R4 `CatalogEntry` to R6 artifacts was found in the supplied package.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A ConceptMap or implementation-guide migration table would improve confidence about which R6 resource/profile/extension should carry each R4 element.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The local package files do not include the ballot discussion or narrative rationale for removing `CatalogEntry`.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Official diff pages, Jira tickets, or change notes would support a stronger justification assessment.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology expansion was not run. The R4 `relation-type` CodeSystem is complete and the same R6 files are absent, so this does not undermine the main removal finding, but it limits certainty about substitute relationship codes.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run a terminology expansion/comparison and search official terminology maps for `triggers` and `is-replaced-by`.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build (`6.0.0-ballot4`), not a final published release. Resource presence or migration guidance may change before final publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the assessment against the final R6 core package when available.
